messages:
anna: thinking out loud — the current autoscaler treats MIG slices as opaque slots. we keep hitting fragmentation when tenants request odd combinations. proposal: make the autoscaler MIG-aware and let the runtime suggest packing hints (preferred splits) to the operator. thoughts?

devon: +1. can you sketch the surface? is this a controller-only change or do we need protocol updates between operator <-> runtime?

anna: controller + small API. idea is: when a pool considers scale-up, operator calls runtime API /packing-hints with candidate node type and list of pending tenant slice requests. runtime returns ranked candidate MIG split configs and an estimated fragmentation delta + warmup penalty. operator chooses node spec to launch.

mike: sounds good but worried about coupling. runtime has load/seq-length signals that affect preferred split (long ctx prefers full GPU). we should keep hints optional so operator can fallback. also need to nail metrics we use for decision-making.

kevin: what about admission-time preemption policy? different splits change preemptibility granularity (e.g., 1/4-MIG vs 1/2-MIG). does the autoscaler need to account for cost of future evictions?

anna: yes. packing-hints should include a simple "eviction_cost" score per split (heuristic: #tenants likely to be preempted * weighted SLO impact). operator can plug that into its cost model.

sophia: edge-case: mixed-tenant workloads where a tenant pins to full-GPU model (large batch) and others use tiny slices. If operator chooses many small slices we may prevent the full-GPU tenant from ever being scheduled. need a soft-reservation signal from scheduler.

tara: +1. we should also expose a "pinning probability" from scheduler/placement layer to the packing-hints call so the runtime knows how often a full-GPU demand appears. otherwise heuristics will be wrong.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: new API schema created: /packing-hints v1 (opt-in). see /ops/api-docs#packing-hints for details.

devon: operational concerns: node spin-up time vs warmup credit. if packing-hints suggests a split that increases warmup time, autoscaler might prefer launching a different node type even if less efficient on steady-state. need explicit tradeoff parameter in cost function.

anna: agreed. propose we return fields: {"split_id", "expected_util_pct", "fragmentation_delta", "warmup_seconds", "eviction_cost"} — then operator has final say.

mike: can we avoid returning too many floats? keep it simple + explain uncertainty band. e.g., expected_util: 40-70%. runtime should annotate confidence.

kevin: implementational note: packing-hints must be cheap (no model loads). use cached sim based on existing catalog benchmarks and current token length distribution. avoid full instantiation.

anna: good call. also: fallback mode where operator provides an explicit "hard constraint" (e.g., must support full-gpu workloads) so runtime filters splits that would block that.

tara: curious about migration path: we have already a bunch of pools with fixed MIG profiles. rollout should be opt-in per pool. operator feature-flag + safe defaults (no change).

sophia: testing plan: 1) sim harness: feed historical admission traces and check fragmentation/utilization delta. 2) small canary pool with mixed tenants. 3) monitor SLO regressions for pinned jobs.

devon: action items?

anna: I can draft a short RFC + API spec w/ example responses. devon: can you add an EMMA sim job for traces? mike/team: can you add a quick cost-model hook in operator to accept the new fields? tara: add rollout plan + feature-flag checklist. kevin: sanity-check eviction_cost heuristic. sophia: design tests. infra-bot: create tracking issue.

infra-bot: ticket #INF-6123 created: "MIG-aware packing hints + autoscaler integration"

mike: timeline suggestion: RFC this week, sim + API prototype next week, canary in two weeks.

anna: thanks — will post RFC draft in #eng-runtime in ~2h. :rocket:
